title: Addressing Mechanical Failure in Heavy Vehicles Leading to Fatal Accidents
what_it_is: Addressing Mechanical Failure in Heavy Vehicles Leading to Fatal Accidents

sections.label: Heavy vehicle accident trends
sections.summary: A MOM and police circular noted rising heavy vehicle accidents, from 816 in 2013 to 877 in 2015, and 22 worker deaths in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In a joint circular issued by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Singapore Police Force, it was noted that there was an increasing trend of fatal and injury accidents involving heavy vehicles, from 816 such accidents in 2013 to 877 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In September 2017, Minister of State for Manpower, Mr Sam Tan, highlighted that in 2016, 22 workers were involved in fatal accidents caused by moving vehicles.

sections.label: Mechanical failure crash statistics
sections.summary: Australian and US reports state mechanical failures accounted for 5% of Australian crash incidents and 12% of US motor vehicle accidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the 2015 Major Accident Investigation Report conducted by the Australian National Truck Accident Research Centre, it was stated that mechanical failures accounted for 5% of crash incidents in Australia, with tyre failure accounting for 72% of losses attributable to mechanical fault.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the US, federal statistics show that mechanical failure plays a role in 12% of all motor vehicle accidents.

sections.label: Vehicle inspection frequency rules
sections.summary: Except omni-buses, inspected every six months, trailers, goods vehicles and other buses are inspected yearly if under 10 years old, otherwise every six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: With the exception of omni-buses, which are inspected every six months, trailers, goods vehicles and all other buses are subject to mandatory inspection only once a year if the vehicle is less than 10 years old, and once every six months if the vehicle is more than 10 years old.

sections.label: No liability for fatal accidents
sections.summary: Non-compliance gives rise to regulatory offences, but no provision pins liability for non-compliance causing fatal accidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Whilst non-compliance of these rules per se give rise to regulatory offences, there is currently no provision that pins liability for non-compliance of the rules giving rise to the fatal accidents.

sections.label: Gaps in investigation and compliance
sections.summary: Mechanical failure may escape investigation under the Road Traffic Act and Workplace Health and Safety Act, and recommendations remain non-mandatory guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As may be evident from the above outline, there is a gap in that, practically speaking, under the current regime, there may be no further investigation if mechanical failure or malfunction had caused the accident since this would likely be beyond the ambit of the Road Traffic Act and the Workplace Health and Safety Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, the limitation lies in the fact that these recommendations remain as non-mandatory guidelines, and there is presently no applicable provision that triggers an investigation and prosecution of owners and operators for not complying with the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is time for us to close these gaps, such as to mandate compliance with the manufacturer's maintenance schedule, the keeping of maintenance records and/or the conduct of daily pre-operational checks.

sections.label: Criminal liability and technology incentives
sections.summary: Without such provisions, imposing criminal liability on corporations is difficult, and a technology fund is suggested to help fleet management systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Without such provisions, it will be difficult to impose criminal liability on corporations and, consequently, there may be not a sufficient motivation to change the corporate culture within the corporations to ensure strict compliance with the maintenance regimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Apart from this, we may also wish to consider incentivising companies to leverage technology to deal with issues of maintenance, for example, the provision of a technology fund to assist in implementing fleet management systems that are able to track maintenance records and alert the owner when a vehicle is due for a periodic inspection in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendation.

sections.label: Road safety after Mr Slemat's death
sections.summary: The speaker hopes proposed measures, once implemented, will make the road safer for road users after Mr Slemat died.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: When Mr Slemat died, the road was not safe for him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: After his death, I do hope that the measures that I have proposed, once implemented, will make the road safer for road users who may otherwise fall victim to accidents caused by mechanical failure.

sections.label: Heavy vehicle statutory lifespan
sections.summary: Most heavy vehicles have a 20-year statutory lifespan, while public buses have a shorter 17-year lifespan because they are very heavily used.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Except for public buses, most heavy vehicles are subject to a maximum statutory lifespan of 20 years, after which they must be deregistered and can no longer be used on our roads.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Public buses are subject to a shorter statutory lifespan of 17 years because they are very heavily used.

sections.label: Penalties for individual employer
sections.summary: For an individual, the employer may face a fine of up to $200,000, imprisonment not exceeding two years, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In the case of an individual, the employer may face a fine of up to $200,000, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or both.

sections.label: Fatal accidents involving heavy vehicles
sections.summary: In 2016 and 2017, there were 85 fatal accidents involving heavy vehicles on-road and on worksites.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In 2016 and 2017, there were a total of 85 fatal accidents involving heavy vehicles both on-road and on worksites – 85 fatal accidents over two years.
